verdicts.strongest_argument: Every number in this claim is verbatim from the 19-May Q1 exhibit, which I fetched and confirmed (802.6 owned + 63.4 customer deposits in digital assets; 905.0 pledged + 100.0 fixed-term in cryptocurrency receivable; loans US$21,140k current + US$33,373k long-term). The fact is correct and the arithmetic checks (1,005 of 1,871 = 53.7% encumbered). But the encumbrance was published in trade press in direct connection with the buyback two days after the announcement: CryptoSlate on 2026-08-06 wrote 'It had also pledged 905 BTC for secured term loans and placed another 100 BTC in a fixed-term product' under the headline 'Canaan can use crypto to buy back nearly 20% of its market value while its core business burns cash' - i.e. the exact 'headline treasury is not free' thesis, in print, with the pledge figure. Two further weaknesses on sizing. First, applying a 2026-03-31 encumbrance split to the 2026-07-31 treasury of 1,917 BTC is an extrapolation the company has not confirmed. Second, and worse for the sign: BTC has gone from $58,504 on 2026-06-30 to $77,934 on 2026-09-03, so US$54.5m of secured loans is now collateralised by ~1,005 BTC worth ~$78m rather than ~$59m - the coverage on the pledge has improved materially since the balance-sheet date, which makes the encumbrance less binding now than when it was published, not more.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Q1 exhibit states 802.6 bitcoins owned plus 63.4 customer deposits, 905.0 pledged for secured term loans and 100.0 in a fixed-term product, with $21,140k current and $33,373k long-term loans.

Draws the encumbrance out explicitly against the buyback: 905 BTC pledged for secured term loans, 100 BTC in a fixed-term product, and the gap between headline treasury value and assets ready for immediate use.
BTC traded at $77,934.11 on 2026-09-03, up from $58,503.73 at 2026-06-30, which raises the collateral coverage on the pledged coins.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The Q1 exhibit that carries these figures is the 2026-05-19 event in the baseline history, which printed -13.66%, the largest absolute move in the eight-row set. The buyback and the CryptoSlate follow-up sit on 2026-08-04 (+12.43%) - the market went UP 12.4% on the day the treasury-as-buyback-currency story broke, and continued to +69.8% over 20 days, which is a market that read the encumbrance disclosure and did not care.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A 2026-06-30 disclosure showing pledged coins materially above 1,005, or new secured borrowing against the treasury that was not in the Q1 exhibit, would make the encumbrance a genuinely new number rather than a restated one.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Both anchors are real and both are public: $7,739k contract liabilities at 2026-03-31 against $9,317k at 2025-12-31 is a line in the 19-May exhibit I fetched, and the 'nearly $87 million ... over 85% from North American clients' comes from the Q3 2025 earnings call, whose transcript is free on Motley Fool. The juxtaposition - a 91% collapse in the funded order book - I could not find drawn out anywhere, and that is the strongest thing about this finding. What kills most of its value is that the implication has already been stated by the company in stronger form and priced: Canaan guided Q2 revenue to $35-45m on 2026-05-19 and the stock fell 13.66% that day. A collapsed order book and a $35-45m guide are the same statement about near-term revenue, and the company's version is the one the market traded on. The 'no new Avalon purchase-order press release between June and September 2026' leg is the weakest part - absence of a discretionary press release is not a disclosure, PO announcements are opportunistic (the Cipher A1566 release was 2024), and the 19-May release did in fact announce a Nordic district-heating win with a 6 MW follow-on order placed in March 2026, so the company was still announcing demand as of the last print. The genuinely unpriced datum is the 2026-06-30 contract-liabilities balance, which arrives at this print, but that is new information arriving rather than a finding about it.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Balance sheet shows contract liabilities of $7,739k at 2026-03-31 versus $9,317k at 2025-12-31.
Q3 2025 call disclosed a contract-advance balance of nearly $87 million with over 85% from North American clients.
'Canaan Shares Dip On Q1 Revenue Miss And Weak Q2 Outlook' - the weak forward demand picture was in wire copy on the day of the Q1 print.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: No separate move is attributable to the order-book decline: it became public inside the 2026-05-19 print (-13.66%), bundled with the guide that says the same thing more directly. Nothing in the +69.8% 20-day run-up is consistent with the market having re-rated on order-book news in either direction.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A 2026-06-30 contract-liabilities balance near zero combined with a Q3 guide below $35m would make this a real earnings driver rather than a restatement of the May guide.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The facts are right but they are in company press releases carried by PR Newswire, Morningstar and StockTitan on the day, and I verified both halves from the filings. The 2026-07-14 6-K exhibit gives June non-JV operating hashrate 3.36 EH/s against installed 10.05 EH/s, 246.2 MW installed capacity, 60.3% average revenue split, and names 'grid maintenance at one of our facilities'. The recovery leg is not in that document - the July update, filed as a 6-K on 2026-08-17, is where operating returns to 10.05 EH/s equal to installed, with 46 BTC mined. So the brief's citation is wrong on the recovery: a 2026-07-14 filing cannot report 2026-07-31 data. The fact survives the citation error, but that is exactly the problem for the finding: monthly operational disclosure is the mechanism that stops a weak Q2 mining line being a surprise. The market has had the June exit rate since 2026-07-14 and the July recovery since 2026-08-17, and the baseline shows +0.69% and -0.43% on those dates - no reaction, because there was nothing to react to. This is the only mitigating claim of the eight and I concede it points the right way, but a self-mining segment that produced $19.1m of a $62.7m Q1 cannot carry much of a $0.36 stock's print when its inputs are already published monthly.

prior_publication.what_it_says: June 2026 update: non-JV operating hashrate 3.36 EH/s vs installed 10.05 EH/s, 246.2 MW, 60.3% average revenue split, grid maintenance at one facility.
6-K carrying the July 2026 production update, in which non-JV operating hashrate is back to 10.05 EH/s equal to installed and 46 BTC were mined.
Wire coverage of the July update: 46 BTC mined, non-JV operating hashrate 10.05 EH/s matching installed, 17.9 J/TH North American fleet efficiency, $0.043/kWh all-in power.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Both source dates are baseline history rows and both are near-zero: 2026-07-15 +0.69% and 2026-08-17 -0.43%. The hosting-agreement capacity step-down (266.3 to 246.2 MW) would have been in the May update published in the 2026-06-24 window (-5.87%), the only date where any of this had a visible cost.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: If Q2 mining revenue prints far below what 3.36 EH/s at a 60.3% split implies, the outage explanation is incomplete and the recovery framing stops being reassuring.

verdicts.strongest_argument: I verified inventory of $139,078k at 2026-03-31 (down from $180,816k), the $22.9m Q1 gross loss and the $35-45m Q2 guide, all in the 19-May exhibit. But the write-down inference is not an inference the market has to make - it has already been made, twice, in public. Press and vendor coverage of the Q1 print stated that the $23m gross loss was 'driven by a $25M non-cash inventory write-down', so the market has seen this exact charge one quarter ago and repriced for it (-13.66%). More damaging: on the Q1 call management said out loud that for older-generation machines 'the company still had some inventory and lowered the price to try to clear that inventory within quarter two' - i.e. management pre-announced a Q2 margin hit on A15-era stock on 2026-05-19. A second write-down is therefore the single most telegraphed item in this print, and it is non-cash, on a stock whose 20-day realised vol is 183% and whose marginal buyer over the last month has been crypto-beta flow following the CLARITY Act rally, not a gross-margin analyst. The self-mining efficiency figures (23.7 J/TH global, 17.9 J/TH North America) are published monthly and are about the mining fleet, not the saleable inventory, so they do not add to the write-down case.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Q1 release: inventory $139,078k at 2026-03-31, gross loss $22.9m on $62.7m revenue, Q2 revenue guided to $35-45m.

Q1 gross loss of $23m attributed to a $25m non-cash inventory write-down, with adjusted gross profit about break-even, and management stating older-generation machines were being price-cut to clear inventory in Q2.
Wire summary of Q1: revenue $62.7m, net loss $88.7m.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The last time this charge landed, the tape gave it -13.66% - the largest move in the baseline's eight rows - so the market has a fresh, priced precedent for exactly this event, and the deadband of 2.25% is a low bar against it. Against that, the stock is +69.8% over 20 days into the print, which is not a tape positioning for a repeat of the May shock.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A write-down materially larger than Q1's $25m, or one that pushes adjusted gross profit clearly negative rather than break-even, would be new rather than telegraphed.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The investing.com leg is not evidence and should be struck. I fetched the page: it lists the 2026-09-08 event under period label 'Q3 2026 (09/2026)' - the wrong quarter, since the release covers the quarter ended 2026-06-30 - with EPS 'actual' -$0.063 and revenue 'actual' $31.20M for an event that has not occurred. That is an auto-populated placeholder. The same column is demonstrably broken for this issuer on real quarters: it carries Q1 2026 EPS 'actual' of -$0.86 against a company-reported GAAP loss of $0.13 per ADS and a net loss of $88.7m on 744.84m ADS (~$0.12/ADS), so the vendor's EPS series is off by roughly 7x and mixes bases. Worse for the claim, if investing.com's $55.41m forecast is genuinely tagged to the 09/2026 quarter, then comparing it to Q2 guidance of $35-45m is apples-to-oranges and the whole 'never marked down' gap may be a labelling artifact. Does the claim survive without that page? Partly, yes, and I concede that: stockanalysis.com independently shows FY2026 revenue consensus of $269.23m from 4 analysts last updated 2026-07-24, and Simply Wall St / Quartr independently show a next-quarter revenue consensus of $53.87m. So consensus above guidance is corroborated. But it is corroborated on free, public, retail-facing pages - which puts it in the published-and-visible band, not the obscure band - and there is a strong counter-example inside the same data: for Q1 the vendor consensus was $64.68m against actual $62.7m 'in line with guidance', i.e. analysts on this name DO mark to guidance, which suggests the $53-55m figure is a stale or mis-tagged aggregate rather than a live view. Finally, the FY arithmetic is less damning than stated: FY $269m against an H1 of ~$103m implies H2 of ~$166m, versus a $196.3m Q4 2025 alone - not an obviously impossible H2 for a rig vendor with BTC back at $77.9k after a +24% August. Sell-side consensus from 4-6 analysts is also not the price-setter on a $261m FPI trading 22m shares a day.

prior_publication.what_it_says: FY2026 revenue consensus $269.23m and EPS -$0.77 from 4 analysts, last updated 2026-07-24 - independent of investing.com.

Lists the 2026-09-08 report under period '09/2026' with EPS actual -$0.063 and revenue actual $31.20M versus $55.41M forecast, for an event that has not happened; the same table shows Q1 2026 EPS actual -$0.86 against a company-reported $0.13 loss per ADS.
Company guided Q2 total revenues to US$35-45m, the number against which any consensus gap is measured, published in the release the market fell 13.66% on.

Benchmark cut its CAN price target to $2 from $3 after the Q1 report, and Rosenblatt cut to $1.30 from $2.25 - sell-side did react to the guide, contradicting the idea that the desks ignored it wholesale.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: There is no option chain and no skew, so no priced statement of magnitude or direction to test this against. The tape gives the opposite of a market braced for a miss: +69.8% over 20 days into the print, -4.37% over the last five days. Note also that the 2026-09-03 timestamp on the investing.com placeholder produced no visible dislocation, which is consistent with it being machine copy nobody trades.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A dated broker note published after 2026-05-19 that still carries a Q2 revenue estimate above $45m, with the analyst named, would turn this from a vendor-aggregate artifact into a real unmarked consensus.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Every 2026-03-31 component here is correct - I confirmed cash $43,451k against $80,778k, loans $21,140k current, 905 BTC pledged against $54.5m of secured term loans - and the BTC print of $58,504 at 2026-06-30 is exact ($58,503.73 per Fortune). But this is the same document and, crucially, the same published aggregation as CAN-h1#0: CryptoSlate on 2026-08-06 put the cash-versus-current-liabilities comparison in print in the same terms the finding uses - '$43.5 million in cash against $106.4 million in current liabilities at March 31' - alongside the 905 pledged BTC and the distinction between headline treasury value and assets ready for use. So the framing is not new. Two things cut the sign. First, the 19-May release also disclosed approximately US$42 million of customer cash collections in April 2026, which the finding omits and which offsets a large share of the $37.3m Q1 burn - the market has had that offset for four months. Second, a 2026-06-30 balance sheet struck at BTC $58,504 is a stale mark: BTC is $77,934 as of 2026-09-03, so the market prices today's ~$159m treasury, not June's ~$119m one, and a weak 6/30 liquidity snapshot is straightforwardly discountable as a low-water mark. Against that, management authorised a $30m crypto-funded buyback on 2026-08-04 and, per stockanalysis.com's news list, management members bought ADS in the open market - both are revealed-preference statements that insiders do not think liquidity is at the wall. What genuinely is unpriced is the 6/30 unencumbered-cash number itself, but 'a new balance sheet arrives at the print' is a description of earnings, not a finding.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Publishes the whole liquidity case: $43.5m cash against $106.4m current liabilities at 3/31, the fall from $80.8m at year-end, 905 BTC pledged, 100 BTC in a fixed-term product, and the ~$42m April customer-receivable collections.
Source of every 3/31 figure in the claim, including the ~$42m April 2026 customer cash collections the claim omits.
BTC closed Q2 2026 at $58,503.73, confirming the mark the claim uses and the size of the subsequent recovery.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The market's response to this exact fact set being published was +12.43% on 2026-08-04 and a +69.8% 20-day run, with the CryptoSlate piece landing on 2026-08-06 inside that run. There is no skew and no implied move, so nothing in the option market is paying for a liquidity accident. Put/call open interest of 0.03 on 6,882 contracts is too thin to read but is certainly not a bid for downside.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A 6/30 unencumbered cash figure below the $21.1m of loans due inside a year, or disclosure of a covenant or margin-call term on the secured loans, would make this the print's driver rather than a restated 3/31 snapshot.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The arithmetic is sound and if anything conservative - I checked it independently. Market cap is $260.70m at $0.35 on 744.84m shares (stockanalysis.com, 2026-09-04 10:52 EDT). Treasury of 1,917 BTC at $77,934 (2026-09-03) is $149.4m, plus 3,952 ETH at ~$2,391-2,495 is ~$9.5-9.9m, so ~$159m - not $165m, because BTC is $77.9k rather than the $81.0k assumed. On the company's own 3-August yardstick that is $159m + $43.5m cash = ~$202.6m against $260.7m, a premium of ~29%, so the claim understates its own case. The problem is that this is the most mechanically visible number in the entire crypto-equity complex: mNAV is computed from two public prices and a public share count, The Block maintains a live CAN treasury page, and the crossover was already written up - ts2.tech published 'Trump Crypto Push Lifts Canaan Stock (CAN) 13% as Treasury Covers 72% of Market Value' in late August, with treasury at $146.1m against a market cap implying ~$202m, i.e. the discount was already reported as gone. On sign, the claim is also contestable: nothing in the 2026-08-04 authorisation conditions the buyback on a discount, the programme runs to 2026-12-12 regardless, monetising crypto at $77.9k buys back more shares per BTC than at $58.5k, and management were buying ADS in the open market. 'The stated rationale no longer holds' is a rhetorical point about a press release, not a cash-flow change.

prior_publication.what_it_says: The buyback exhibit itself, stating ~US$130m of digital assets as of 2026-08-03 and the below-treasury-plus-cash rationale referenced to 2026-03-31.

Headline and body report the treasury at $146.1m covering 72.3% of market capitalisation after a 13% CLARITY-Act-driven jump, i.e. the discount had already inverted and was published (page returned 403 to direct fetch; content read from search result summary, marked snippet_only).
Market cap $260.70m, price $0.35, 744.84m shares outstanding as of 2026-09-04, plus a news item that management members bought ADS in the open market.
Maintains a live public page for Canaan's bitcoin holdings, so treasury-versus-market-cap is continuously computed for anyone watching.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The +69.8% 20-day move that created the premium is itself the priced statement - the market bid this stock through its own treasury value with full knowledge of the treasury, on a publicly attributed crypto-policy catalyst. A market that did not know the premium existed could not have created it.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: If management state on the call that they will not monetise crypto at current levels, or disclose that zero ADS were repurchased under the authorisation, the withdrawal of the bid becomes an event rather than an inference.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The facts check out against the filing: I confirmed the 2027-01-11 deadline after a 180-day extension, the $1.00-for-ten-consecutive-business-days test, and 1 ADS = 15 Class A ordinary shares; +186% from $0.3501 is correct arithmetic. It is also true that the 8 September call is the first scheduled management appearance since 2026-07-15, since the monthly production updates are press releases with no call. But the whole situation is published and was covered on the day by Yahoo Finance and Blockspace, and the company's own release says it 'intends to continue monitoring the closing bid price ... and will evaluate all available options during the second compliance period' - so the need for a capital-structure action is stated by the issuer, in public, and the market's response was +0.69%. This is the textbook case of structural-and-known: a sub-$1 Nasdaq name with an ADS-ratio lever and a stated deadline is about as far from novel as a finding gets, and age is not novelty. The November notice timing is the hunter's own inference and not published, which is the finding's one real contribution, but it also argues against reaching this print - nothing obliges management to announce a ratio change on 8 September, the deadline is four months out, and the 2027-01-11 date sits two quarters beyond this window. On top of that, an ADS-ratio change is value-neutral by construction, and the +113.76% move off the 52-week low shows a tape on which a further +186% over four months is not the arithmetic impossibility the claim asserts.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Announces the additional 180-day compliance period through 2027-01-11, the $1.00 for ten consecutive business days test, the 1 ADS = 15 Class A ordinary shares ratio, and that the company will evaluate all available options.
'Canaan gets 180-day Nasdaq extension to regain $1 bid price' - the deadline was in mainstream wire copy on the day.
Reports the extension to 2027-01-11, notes each ADS represents 15 ordinary shares, and states the filing does not propose or authorise a reverse split.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The date the deadline was granted, 2026-07-15, is a baseline history row with a move of +0.69% - the market was handed the deadline and did nothing with it. The absence of any option chain means there is no priced probability of a ratio action either way.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: An extraordinary-general-meeting notice, a depositary-agreement amendment filing, or explicit ratio-change language in the 8 September release would move this from known-structural to a dated event inside the window.

interactions: Four of the eight rest on one document, the 2026-05-19 Q1 release (SEC exhibit tm2614943d2_ex99-1.htm and its PR Newswire twin): CAN-h1#0 (BTC encumbrance and the $54.5m of loans), CAN-h1#1 (contract liabilities $7.739m/$9.317m), CAN-h1#3 (inventory $139.1m, $22.9m gross loss, the $35-45m guide) and CAN-h2#1 (cash $43.5m, current liabilities $106.4m, the same 905 pledged BTC). CAN-h2#0 is a fifth derivative of it, since its entire gap is measured against that release's guidance. The sharpest collapse is CAN-h1#0 and CAN-h2#1: they cite the identical sentence about 905 pledged coins and $54.5m of secured term loans, and both are answered by one article, CryptoSlate 2026-08-06, which aggregates the pledge, the cash fall from $80.8m to $43.5m and the $106.4m of current liabilities in a single piece. Those two are one fact seen twice and must not be double-counted; I would score the pair jointly at roughly -3.5% to -4% total, not the sum of my two individual sizes. CAN-h1#1 and CAN-h1#3 also converge on one conclusion - Q2/H2 revenue and gross margin collapse - which the company already stated as guidance, so they share their priced-in mass with each other and with CAN-h2#0. There is a genuine sign conflict between CAN-h1#0/CAN-h2#1 and CAN-h2#2: the first pair argues the treasury is worth less than headline because it is encumbered, the second argues the stock now trades at a premium to that same treasury. Both can be true, but they cannot both be sized fully - if the usable treasury is smaller, the premium in CAN-h2#2 is larger and the two findings are billing the same bearish dollar twice. Separately, both encumbrance findings are undercut by the same fact that funds CAN-h2#2's premium: BTC at $77,934 on 2026-09-03 versus $58,504 at 2026-06-30 improves the pledge coverage while inflating the market-cap-to-NAV gap. CAN-h1#2 is the only mitigating claim and it partially offsets CAN-h1#3 and CAN-h2#1 by giving a published, already-reversed cause for a weak Q2 mining line. Finally, CAN-h1#2's citation is internally wrong - the 2026-07-31 recovery data it attributes to the 2026-07-14 filing is in fact in the 2026-08-17 6-K - and CAN-h2#0 rests in part on an investing.com page whose 'actual' Q2 revenue of $31.20m is a pre-print placeholder for an event that has not happened, mislabelled as period 09/2026, on a table whose EPS column is off by roughly 7x for Q1 2026. Neither error destroys the underlying fact, but both were checkable against the primary document and were not checked.
